q: 1. The edge of drawing board where T-square is made to slide is called
explain: The working edge (or ebony edge) is a perfectly straight wooden strip on the left side of the drawing board used to guide the T-square.

q: 2. The needle point of the compass should be…… the lead point.
explain: The needle point must be slightly longer than the pencil lead so the needle penetrates the paper while the lead still touches the surface to draw the arc.

q: 3. Drawing board is made of
explain: Softwood like white pine or fir is used because it allows drawing pins to be inserted and removed easily, and 'seasoning' prevents warping.

q: 4. Drawing equipment used by draftsmen primarily as a guide for drawing horizontal lines on a drafting table is
explain: The T-square's blade slides along the working edge of the drawing board, providing a reliable guide for drawing horizontal lines.

q: 5. Set squares are not used to draw
explain: Horizontal lines are primarily drawn using the T-square or a mini-drafter; set squares are typically used for vertical and inclined lines relative to the T-square.

q: 6. For drawing large-size circles .................. is attached to the compass (>150mm).
explain: A lengthening bar is an extension that increases the radius of the compass beyond its standard limit.

q: 7. Circles of small radii are drawn by means of a
explain: Bow compasses are rigid and small, making them ideal for maintaining precision while drawing small circles.

q: 8. Which one is not drafting equipment?
explain: All listed items (drafter, scale, and even a dust cloth to keep the sheet clean) are considered part of the drafting environment.

q: 9. Circles of very small radii are drawn by means of a
explain: A drop compass is specifically used for very tiny circles, where the center point remains fixed while the pencil lead 'drops' and rotates around it.

q: 10. For drawing thin lines of uniform thickness the pencil should be sharpened in the form of -
explain: A chisel edge is used for drawing long, thin, uniform lines (like outlines) because the wide edge wears down more slowly than a point.

q: 11. Parallel ruling straight edge machine is used to draw
explain: A parallel ruling straight-edge is a drafting machine attachment that slides vertically on wires/cords while remaining horizontal, used primarily to draw horizontal parallel lines.

q: 12. To remove unnecessary lines ....... is used
explain: The standard tool for correcting errors or removing construction lines is an eraser.

q: 13. Uses of the T-square, set squares, scale and protractor are combined in the
explain: A drafting machine (or mini-drafter) is an all-in-one tool that replaces several individual drafting instruments.

q: 14. Circle and arcs of circles are drawn by means of a .......
explain: A compass is the primary instrument used for drawing circular geometry.

q: 15. Inking pen is used for drawing ----------- in ink
explain: While technical pens can be used for many things, traditional inking pens were primarily used with guides to draw permanent straight lines.

q: 16. The edge of the board on which T-square is made to slide is called .............
explain: The left (or designated) straight edge of the drawing board, along which the T-square's stock slides, is called the working edge.

q: 17. A drafter helps in drawing .............
explain: A drafter (drafting machine) is designed mainly to draw parallel and perpendicular lines quickly and accurately using its scale arms set at fixed angles.

q: 18. Set squares are used to draw
explain: Used alone or with a T-square, set squares can draw vertical lines, inclined lines at fixed angles, and sets of parallel lines.

q: 19. Which pencil is used for thinner line ?
explain: The 'H' stands for Hardness. Higher numbers (like 2H) have harder lead, which produces thinner, lighter lines.

q: 20. To draw smooth curves of any nature, drafting instrument used is .............
explain: A French curve is a flexible-shaped template specifically designed to help draw smooth irregular curves that are not simple arcs of a circle.

q: 21. Parallel lines can be drawn with the help of .............
explain: Parallel lines can be drawn using a mini-drafter, a T-square (sliding along the board edge), or a pair of set squares (one sliding against the other), so all listed tools work.

q: 22. Stock of T-square makes an angle with working edge
explain: The stock is fixed perpendicular (90°) to the blade so it registers squarely against the board's working edge.

q: 23. The needle point of the compass should be .......than the lead point
explain: The needle point is set slightly longer so it stays anchored in the paper while the lead point traces the circle.

q: 24. Parallel ruling straight edge machine is used to draw
explain: The parallel ruling straight edge slides vertically on the board to draw a series of accurate horizontal lines.

q: 25. Mechanical lines are types of
options: line of drawn with free hand
explain: Mechanical lines refer to precise lines created using instruments like scales and T-squares rather than free-hand sketching.

q: 26. The letter 'H' labeled in a drawing pencil indicates .............
explain: The 'H' grading on pencils denotes relative hardness of the graphite lead — a higher number before H (e.g., 4H) means a harder, lighter lead, useful for fine, thin lines.

q: 27. The artificial light on the drawing board should be diffused light from the .............
explain: For a right-handed drafter, artificial light should come from the left side (diffused) to prevent the drafting hand and instruments from casting shadows over the working area.

q: 28. In Engineering Drawing, French curves mean
options: drafting tools used to draw non-linear drawings
drafting tools used to draw oblong figures
explain: French curves are drafting templates of varying curvature used to draw smooth non-linear (irregular curved) lines.

q: 29. The following instrument is not used for drawing straight line .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'straight edge' is marked as not used for drawing straight lines in this context; set-squares and the board's working edge are the standard tools/guides actually used for ruling straight lines.

q: 30. Vertical lines are drawn .............
explain: The standard drafting convention for drawing vertical lines (especially freehand or with a T-square/set-square) is to draw from top to bottom for better control and visibility.

q: 31. The drawing prepared by a pencil and without use of drawing instrument is called
explain: Freehand sketching relies solely on the artist's eye and hand coordination without tools like rulers or compasses.

q: 32. *In Engineering Drawing, French Curves mean :
options: drafting tools used to draw non-linear figures
drafting tools used to draw oblong figures
explain: French curves are plastic or wooden templates used in manual drafting to draw smooth, non-circular curves that cannot be drawn with a compass.

q: 33. Eraser shield is best used in .............
explain: An eraser shield, which protects surrounding lines while erasing a specific area, is especially useful in detailed hand-drawn perspective drawings where selective correction is often needed without disturbing adjacent linework.

q: 34. Pencil drawings are generally corrected or revised with the help of :
explain: An eraser shield is a thin metal or plastic template that allows a drafter to erase small areas without disturbing the surrounding lines.
A graphos is a type of pen with an interchangeable metal nib used for both drawing and lettering (writing) on technical drawings, making it a drawing-and-writing instrument.

q: 36. What is used for drawing curves which can not drawn by compass
explain: French curves are used to draw smooth irregular curves that cannot be produced with a compass.

q: 37. The equipment used to draft vertical and angular line is .............
explain: Vertical and angular (inclined) lines are drawn using a set square placed against the T-square's blade, combining both tools together.

q: 38. Uses of the T-square, set squares, scale and protractor are combined in the .............
explain: A drafting machine integrates the functions of the T-square, set squares, scale, and protractor into a single adjustable device mounted on the drawing board.

q: 39. Circle and arcs are drawn by means of a .............
explain: A compass, with its adjustable pivot and pencil/pen leg, is the standard instrument used to draw circles and arcs of a given radius.

q: 40. Clinograph is a type of .............
explain: A clinograph is an adjustable set square whose angle can be varied and fixed as required, functioning as a specialized (adjustable) type of set square.

q: 41. Set square are used to draw .............
explain: Set squares, used alone or in combination with a T-square, can draw vertical lines, inclined lines (at fixed standard angles), and parallel lines, so all of these apply.

q: 42. The hardness of the pencil lead increase as numeral letter H .............
explain: In pencil grading, a higher number preceding 'H' (e.g., 4H vs 2H) indicates progressively harder, lighter graphite lead, so hardness increases as the H-number increases.

q: 43. The needle point of the compass should be ............. than the lead point.
explain: The compass's steel needle point should be kept slightly shorter than the pencil lead point so the pencil tip makes full contact with the paper while the needle firmly anchors the center.

q: 44. Chisel pencils are used to draw .............
explain: A pencil sharpened to a chisel edge maintains a consistent line width when guided along a straightedge, making it best suited for drawing straight lines of uniform thickness.

q: 45. To draw or measure angles, we use .............
explain: A protractor is the dedicated instrument specifically designed for accurately drawing and measuring angles on a drawing.
